children: NATIONAL BEVERAGE CORP reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 results with revenue essentially flat at $330.7M versus $330.5M a year earlier, while net income fell to $47M and diluted EPS declined to $0.5 amid rising packaging and ingredient costs.
Revenue was $330.7M for Q1 FY2027, essentially flat versus $330.5M in the year-ago quarter (average selling price up 7.1%, case volume down 6.4%).
Net income was $47.0M for Q1 FY2027, down from $55.8M in the year-ago quarter.
Diluted EPS was $0.50 for Q1 FY2027, versus $0.60 in the year-ago quarter.
Revenue Trend: Net sales were flat as a 7.1% increase in average selling price offset a 6.4% decline in case volume.
Brand Momentum: Power+ and the company's carbonated brands were affected by price increases and lower volumes; LaCroix and Rip It remain core brands.
Cost Pressure & Margin Impact: Gross margin fell to 35.0%, with higher packaging and ingredient costs—aluminum pressures accounted for roughly a 600 basis-point headwind.
Operations & Seasonality: Sales are seasonal with summer strength; the company operates a hybrid DSD and warehouse distribution model to support broad retail coverage.
Liquidity-Driven Action: The company paid a $304.2M special dividend, which reduced working capital and the current ratio and affected near-term operating liquidity.
